description: Biometric Embedding Leakage and Rank-1 Re-Identification Assessment

literature_review_citations.citation: Mai, G., Cao, K., Yuen, P. C., & Jain, A. K. (2018). On the reconstruction of face images from deep face templates. IEEE T-BIOM, 1(1), 118-131.
literature_review_citations.finding: Demonstrated that deep feature representations (such as 128-D/512-D embeddings) can be inverted via trained deconvolutional neural networks to reconstruct recognizable, human-identifiable facial imagery with over 90% matching TAR against genuine galleries.

literature_review_citations.citation: Cole, F., Belanger, D., Krishnan, D., Sarna, A., Inbar, I., & Freeman, W. T. (2017). Synthesizing normalized faces from facial identity representations. CVPR 2017.
literature_review_citations.finding: Proved direct synthesis of photorealistic, pose-normalized frontal facial portraits from high-level face recognition embeddings.

incident_runbook_consequence: CRITICAL DPDPA CLASSIFICATION: Raw embeddings are legally deemed sensitive biometric personal data. A database dump of embeddings constitutes a mandatory reportable personal data breach under DPDPA Section 8(6), regardless of whether keyed rotation was applied.
